newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY RADIO NOON HEADLINES - SEPT 23.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY RADIO NOON HEADLINES - SEPT 23.

text.p: These are the main headlines on Hungary's Kossuth Radio midday news. Reuters cannot vouch for their accuracy:

- The goverment wants to introduce a compulsory minimum consultancy fee for visits to the doctor in an attempt to curb the spiralling the social security deficit, which has already reached 100 billion forints.
- The health insurance authorities have expressed opposition to planned cuts in drugs subsidies as it would result in a 10 percent increase in the price of medicines.
- The governing Socialists plan to divert 40 billion forints from this year's budget to cover the privatisation commitments
- The police strongly deny reports that drug dealers tried to sell LSD-impregnated stamps to kindergarten children.

- An agreement has been signed between the Securities and Stock Exchange supervisory bodies and the Consumer Protection Agency to tighten securities trade regulations to curb fraud and money-laundering.
